name: California
note: In California the funeral director registers the death with the local registrar through CA-EDRS within 8 calendar days, and before disposition. The attending physician certifies the cause within 15 hours, or the coroner does so for reportable deaths. Registration gates the disposition permit. Authorized certified copies are restricted, but informational copies are available to anyone. Deaths reach the voter roll three ways: county death lists to the county elections official, the State Registrar's copies of out-of-county deaths, and the Secretary of State's matching of CDPH death records in the statewide voter file; the State Registrar also has birth records of the deceased marked. Federal benefit agencies are reached through the State's EDR feed to SSA (federal layer). The Health and Safety Code itself still could not be read, so the registration chain rests on recollection; only the regulations (read on law.cornell.edu) are verified.

steps.title: Death determined under the Uniform Determination of Death Act
steps.who: A physician (or other person authorised to pronounce) determining death by cessation of circulatory and respiratory, or of all brain, functions.
steps.summary: California adopts the Uniform Determination of Death Act. The place where death is officially pronounced sets the registration district.

steps.title: Informant supplies personal particulars to the funeral director
steps.who: Next of kin or another informant.
steps.summary: The funeral director gathers the decedent's personal data from an informant to complete the certificate.

steps.title: Attending physician completes the medical certification within 15 hours
steps.summary: The physician completes and attests the medical and health section and the time of death within 15 hours after the death, unless the coroner must be notified.

steps.title: Reportable deaths go to the coroner
steps.who: The physician, funeral director or other person with knowledge of a reportable death.
steps.trigger: A death in a category the coroner must investigate (violent, sudden or unusual, unattended, and so on).
steps.summary: The Health and Safety Code lists the deaths to be reported to the coroner, and the Government Code makes it the coroner's duty to inquire into and determine their circumstances, manner and cause.

steps.title: Coroner completes the medical certification
steps.who: The county coroner or medical examiner.
steps.summary: In coroner cases the coroner, not the attending physician, completes the cause-of-death section of the certificate.

steps.title: Funeral director registers the death with the local registrar within 8 calendar days
steps.who: The funeral director (or the person acting as one) in charge of the remains.
steps.trigger: Completion of the certificate; before disposition.

deadline.text: within 8 calendar days after death and prior to any disposition

steps.summary: Each death must be registered with the local registrar of births and deaths for the district where death was pronounced or the body was found, within 8 calendar days after death and before any disposition. Registration is done through the California Electronic Death Registration System (CA-EDRS). Separately, a regulation (verified) lets the local and State registrars accept a death record for ordinary registration only if the local registrar receives it within one year of the death; later records go through the delayed-registration chapters of the Health and Safety Code.

steps.title: Local registrar issues the disposition permit
steps.who: The local registrar of births and deaths.
steps.summary: A permit for disposition is issued once the certificate is registered, so registration gates burial or cremation.

steps.title: Authorized certified copies are restricted; informational copies are open
steps.who: The State Registrar or a local registrar or county recorder.
steps.trigger: Application, with a sworn statement for an authorized copy.
steps.summary: Only listed persons (close relatives, legal representatives, funeral directors, certain agencies, people with a court order) may obtain an authorized certified copy. Anyone else gets an informational certified copy marked as not valid to establish identity.

steps.title: Registrar notifies the county elections official of deceased persons
steps.who: The local registrar of births and deaths (or county health officer).
steps.trigger: Registration of deaths of persons of voting age.
steps.summary: Deaths are reported monthly to the county elections official, who cancels the affidavits of registration of deceased voters. The Secretary of State's regulations confirm that county elections officials process county death records under Elections Code section 2205, but the monthly cadence and the sender rest on section 2205 itself, which could not be read.

steps.title: State Registrar copies out-of-county death notices to the county elections official
steps.who: The State Registrar of Vital Statistics, to the county elections official at the address the county gives the Secretary of State each January.
steps.trigger: The State Registrar's notice to a county's local registrar of residents of that county who died in another county (Health and Safety Code section 102245).
steps.summary: When the State Registrar tells a local registrar about residents who died outside the county, it must send a copy of that notice to the county elections official, so deaths away from home also reach the voter roll. The regulation ties the copy to the Health and Safety Code notice, whose cadence could not be read.

steps.title: CDPH death records matched against the statewide voter registration system (VoteCal)
steps.who: The California Department of Public Health supplies death records; the Secretary of State matches them in the statewide voter registration system and sends potential matches to the county elections official, who confirms and cancels.
steps.trigger: Receipt by the Secretary of State of new death records from CDPH, and any new or updated voter registration record.
steps.summary: Each batch of CDPH death records the Secretary of State receives is compared with the statewide voter file, and each new or updated registration is compared with CDPH death records. A potential match goes to the county elections official, and a confirmed match is cancelled. The regulation sets no cadence for CDPH's records; the statute that governs it was not read.

steps.title: Birth records of deceased persons marked by the local registrar
steps.who: The State Registrar notifies the local registrar or county recorder holding the birth record; local registrars may also match local deaths to local births themselves.
steps.trigger: Notification by the State Registrar that a person whose birth is registered in the local office has died.
steps.summary: On the State Registrar's notice, the local registrar or county recorder notes the death in the birth index or on the birth record, with the death certificate number, and reports any request for a deceased person's birth certificate that claims to be the applicant's own. The regulation sets no time for the State Registrar's notice.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Within 8 calendar days after death and before disposition (not verified against the statute text in this pass).

informantDuty.note: The funeral director completes and registers the certificate; the informant only supplies particulars.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of ordinary certificates; the coroner sees only reportable deaths.

electronicRegistration.note: Statewide CA-EDRS, used by funeral directors, physicians and coroners. The statutory basis was not confirmed.

certificateAccess.note: Authorized certified copies only to listed persons on a sworn statement; informational certified copies (marked as not valid to establish identity) to anyone.

gaps: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov still answers every request with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge (HTTP 403, 28 October 2026), an anti-automation control that was left alone, so no California statute text (Health and Safety, Government, Elections or Probate Code) could be read. law.cornell.edu carries the California Code of Regulations but not the codes. All nine original steps and all five features rest on recollection of the codes and stay unverified; section numbers (HSC 7180, 102775, 102780, 102800, 102850, 102860, 103050, 103525, 103526; Gov. Code 27491; Elec. Code 2205) need confirming from the text.

No official agency page quoting the Health and Safety Code could be reached: www.cdph.ca.gov, ca.gov, www.sos.ca.gov, www.dhcs.ca.gov, www.dmv.ca.gov, www.ftb.ca.gov, oal.ca.gov, www.courts.ca.gov, the Cemetery and Funeral Bureau (www.cfb.ca.gov) and the county hosts tried (www.lacounty.gov, publichealth.lacounty.gov, rrcc.lacounty.gov, www.sandiegocounty.gov, www.sccgov.org) all refuse the session at the egress proxy (CONNECT 403), as does govt.westlaw.com, the official CCR publisher. CA-EDRS guidance and California's EDR feed to SSA under 42 U.S.C. 405(r) remain unsourced.

The California Code of Regulations was searched on law.cornell.edu for the registration chain: Title 17 (Public Health) division 1 chapter 1 subchapter 4 (Records and Statistics, sections 902 to 916) and Title 16 divisions 12 and 23 (Cemetery and Funeral Bureau) contain nothing on the medical certification deadline, the funeral director's filing deadline, coroner referral or disposition permits. Regulation 17 CCR 908's one-year limit is the only time limit found and is not the registration deadline.

The cadence of the out-of-county death notice (HSC 102245, referenced by 2 CCR 20075), of CDPH's death records to the Secretary of State (2 CCR 19079), and of the State Registrar's notice to the birth-record office (2 CCR 910) is set, if anywhere, in statute that could not be read, so those three pushes carry latency null.

No California provision was found or verified for death notification to the DMV, the Franchise Tax Board or Medi-Cal (DHCS). The Medi-Cal estate recovery notice duty (Prob. Code 9202) was not checked.
The exact deadline for the coroner's certification (believed to be 3 days after examination under HSC 102860) and the list of reportable deaths in HSC 102850 were not read.
The features centralPopulationRegister, governmentPropagation and privateSectorVerification are not recorded for California.
